Theme

Death philosophy quotes

Philosophy quotes about death confront mortality, fear, legacy, and what a finite life can mean.

8 passages · 7+ thinkers in this selection

Why this theme matters

Some argue that death is nothing to us; others that mortality intensifies value; still others that grief and remembrance are ethical tasks. The theme sits between metaphysics and consolation.

In the history of philosophy

Epicurean therapy, Stoic rehearsals of mortality, Platonic immortality debates, and Buddhist attention to impermanence remain touchstones.

Thinkers in this collection

Epicurus , Seneca , Marcus Aurelius , Lucretius , Michel de Montaigne , Plato , Baruch Spinoza

Frequently asked questions

What do philosophers say about death?

They ask whether death harms the one who dies, how fear of death should be handled, and what duties the living owe the dead.

Is fear of death irrational?

Some schools say yes if death is non-existence; others treat fear as informative about attachment and unfinished responsibility.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about death?

This theme gathers English passages from Stoic, Epicurean, Chinese, and modern sources.

  1. Death is nothing to us: for what has been dissolved has no sensation, and what has no sensation is nothing to us.
    Epicurus
    Epicureanism
  2. He who has learned how to die has unlearned how to be a slave.
    Seneca
    Stoicism
  3. Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Stoicism
  4. Therefore death is nothing to us, and does not concern us at all.
    Lucretius
    Epicureanism
  5. To philosophize is to learn how to die.
    Michel de Montaigne
    Renaissance Humanism
  6. Depart then in peace; the one who releases you is also at peace.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Stoicism
  7. This very practice of philosophers is a release and separation of soul from body.
    Plato
    Platonism
  8. A free man thinks of nothing less than of death.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Rationalism
